Stated Claim / Post Context:
Controversial One Nation cartoon showing Australian politicians being deliberately mowed down by a car resurfaces after horrific attack on MP Helen Haines - sparking fiery debate

A controversial One Nation cartoon depicting Australian politicians being deliberately mowed down by a vehicle has resurfaced.

Actual Article Body:
By DAILY MAIL

Published:  07:47 AEDT, 23 October 2026   |  Updated:  07:53 AEDT, 23 October 2026

A controversial One Nation cartoon depicting Australian politicians being deliberately mowed down by a vehicle has resurfaced following the alleged attack on independent MP Helen Haines, sparking a heated debate over whether the political satire has gone too far.

Titled The State of Melbourne, the two year old One Nation-produced cartoon shows animated versions of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and former Victorian premier Daniel Andrews being struck by a vehicle.

The video begins with a reference to Andrews' involvement in a collision with a teenage cyclist before taking a darker turn, showing a vehicle deliberately running down politicians and familiar Australian characters, including Robert Irwin and Bluey.

The video has sparked a heated debate following the alleged attack on Haines, with some Australians demanding it be removed and others defending it as political satire.

'There are better, mature, less violent, less aggressive ways to deliver a message,' one said.

A second added: 'Gutter politics at it’s worst. She doesn’t deserve to be a senator. Shes a disgrace to Australian politics. Just when you thought she couldn’t get any lower.'

But others argued the cartoon was being unfairly criticised over an incident that occurred years after its release.

'What happened was horrific, but are you for real? A cartoon that came out long before it happened,' one Aussie said.

A controversial One Nation cartoon depicting Australian politicians being deliberately mowed down by a vehicle has resurfaced following the alleged attack on independent MP Helen Haines, sparking a heated debate over whether the political satire has gone too far

The cartoon was first published by One Nation two years ago - but has resurfaced in the wake of the Helen Haines attack with many Aussies saying it went too far

Another added: 'Remember when Australia could laugh and not be so politically correct? These videos are hilarious.'

A third said: 'Oh now, One Nation can predict the future through cartoons? And I only thought the Simpson's could do that!'

Dr Haines underwent the amputation of both her legs after 43-year-old Brendan Nugent allegedly deliberately struck her with his four-wheel drive.

She remains in a critical condition in Melbourne's Alfred Hospital.

The alleged attack took place on Monday outside Dr Haines' electoral office in Wangaratta, about three hours northeast of Melbourne.

Nugent, who neighbours have said lived alone on a remote property in nearby Tarrawingee, appeared briefly in court on Wednesday charged with offences including dangerous driving causing serious harm.

His lawyer Chirag Patel told the court Nugent had not previously been diagnosed with any mental health issues, but he was concerned for his client's psychological wellbeing and wanted him assessed.

The motivations which led Nugent to allegedly carry out the attack are unclear.

There is no suggestion the video influenced the alleged attack on Haines or that the two incidents are linked.

Senator Hanson was forced to apologise for her cartoon mocking Jacqui Lambie's health battle with vaginal prolapse

It's not the first time a One Nation cartoon has sparked controversy this week.

Pauline Hanson was forced to apologise after the party's latest Please Explain cartoon was accused of mocking independent senator Jacqui Lambie's struggle with vaginal prolapse.

The animation sparked backlash from politicians across the political divide, with Lambie publicly condemning One Nation on Monday.

Speaking in Tasmania that same day, Hanson initially dismissed the criticism, telling Lambie to 'get over it'.

'Jacqui Lambie, get over it... it is actually satirical.'

'I think she's taken it to heart, which she shouldn't be. You know, have a good look at it, and have a bit of a laugh Jacqui, and lighten up,' she added.

But by Tuesday, Hanson had reversed her position and issued an apology, claiming she had not seen the cartoon before it was published.

'The video went up without me actually seeing it, and I was not aware of its content. I have spoken to the creator of that video and I've asked him to actually change it,' Senator Hanson told News24.

'I respect people's views and opinions out there and it wasn't as tastefully done as it could have been. And I do apologise for that, and I've already spoken to them about changing it.'

President Donald Trump backs Vivek Ramaswamy on controversial ad featuring Democrat Amy Acton’s estranged mother

President Donald Trump said that Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee for Ohio governor, should keep running a controversial ad featuring the estranged mother of Democratic opponent Amy Acton.

Actual Article Body:
eNewspaper

Sign up for email newsletters

Sign up for email newsletters

eNewspaper

Trending:

COLUMBUS, Ohio — President Donald Trump said Thursday that Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee for Ohio governor, should keep running a controversial ad featuring the estranged mother of Democratic opponent Amy Acton, posting on social media that it was “hitting pay dirt.”

Trump also denounced Ohio Republican Gov. Mike DeWine, who criticized the ad as “deeply, deeply troubling” earlier in the day. Acton previously served in DeWine’s administration as a health official. Her mother lost custody of Acton and her brother after her husband — the children’s stepfather — was indicted for raping Acton.

Illinois first lady MK Pritzker commits $500,000 to Ohio’s Amy Acton after Ramaswamy ad featuring her mother

“He strongly suggested that Vivek should, ‘take down the Ad,’” Trump wrote. “He probably wants a Dumocrat to win, and certainly doesn’t want someone who will do a much better job than he is capable of doing. I suggested, on the other hand, that Vivek should keep it up, and let everyone listen to the mother of a defective, dishonest, and incapable Candidate, explain how the daughter is a DISASTER who, uncontrollably, lies, cheats, and steals!”

At a gathering with reporters at the Ohio Statehouse, DeWine recalled the painful experiences of rape victims he dealt with as a county prosecutor and state attorney general.

“It’s wrong to run this ad,” he said. “And, even at this late time — my wife, Fran, saw the ad just run this morning on TV — I would just urge the Ramaswamy campaign to take this down.”

The term-limited DeWine’s remarks place him at odds with Ramaswamy, whom he has endorsed. The biotech entrepreneur and former presidential candidate plans to spend $4 million to broadcast it online and on television.

But the governor stopped short of pulling his backing of the Republican for now. DeWine recalled a previous line of attack by the Acton campaign had mentioned Ramaswamy’s mother and said that also was wrong — “family members have always historically been off limits” — though he noted it was never used in a multimillion-dollar ad campaign.

That critique from the summer cited an investigative report into Geetha Ramaswamy’s role at a pharmaceutical company run by her son, who Acton and Democrats described as “hiring his own mother to manipulate clinical trial data.”

The Ramaswamy campaign called those claims “slanderous” and said he’s being held to a different standard than Acton and other Democrats who have attacked Republicans’ families.

“Governor DeWine is correct that the first and only candidate to attack the mother of her opponent in this race was Amy Acton,” spokesperson Connie Luck said in a statement, adding, “We refuse to accept the media’s double standards.”

By chiming in, DeWine has entered the fray of a growing rift among Ohio Republicans over the advertisement — as both the governor’s race and a race for U.S. Senate appear far tighter than expected in a state Donald Trump won handily three times. The video features Acton’s birth mother, Donna Arthur, calling her “a liar” and insinuating she has mental health issues.

Acton, Ohio’s COVID-19-era health director, has made no secret of facing homelessness and abuse as a child. Arthur lost custody of her children after their stepfather, Arthur’s husband, was indicted on a charge of rape involving Acton. Acton’s campaign on Tuesday posted a video of her brother, who supported her backstory about living in a tent and being abused.

Republican Vice President JD Vance, an Ohio native son, expressed disgust during an Ohio campaign swing Wednesday with Republicans “whining” about the ad as low and in poor taste. But Republican U.S. Sen. Jon Husted, DeWine’s former lieutenant governor — running in a tight retention race against Democrat Sherrod Brown — has said he would not have run the ad, as has Republican Secretary of State Frank LaRose, who is running for state auditor.

Another influential Ohio Republican, former U.S. Rep. Jim Renacci, posted a lengthy essay on X overnight, suggesting that “the floor may have just fallen out from under the Republican campaign for Ohio Governor” and urging every Republican to distance themselves from it.

Amid the turmoil, Ohio Republican Party Chairman Alex Triantafilou posted what sounded like a warning, or a threat.

“The final days of a tough campaign are always the best time to find out who is really with you and who just posts and pretends,” he wrote. “Yes—we are keeping score.” The quote was followed by a winking-eye emoji.

The ad is also dividing Republicans nationally.

Nikki Haley, who sparred with Ramaswamy during the 2024 Republican presidential primary over the personal nature of his attacks, called him “a bad guy” in a social media post Tuesday. “It’s a shame he continues to get away with it,” she wrote.

At the same time, Media Matters for America, a left-leaning media watchdog group, has reported that many within the national conservative media are promoting and praising the ad. Ramaswamy’s campaign manager, Jonathan Ewing, characterized it as “a campaign-ending moment for Amy Acton.”

Wayne Allyn Root, of Gateway Pundit, called it “absolutely hilarious” and Daily Wire host Michael Knowles described it as “brilliant.”

Police and court records show Cledith Arthur was arrested and charged with the rape of Acton in July 1978, when she was 12, after her biological father lodged a formal complaint against him. The abuse allegedly happened from December 1976 to April 1978. Cledith Arthur failed to show for a court appearance and became a fugitive.

Donna Arthur remained married to him until his death in 2004.
